item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Awesome.
This actually makes me recall a discussion I once had when I was still actively playing tabletop RPGs in the WoD universe.
At one point there were so many settings, and theme/clan/brood books in circulation that it seemed that pretty much every person in the world was either a vampire, a mage, a mummie, a ghost, a werecreature, some mutated abomination or a fairy. And if they weren't that, they were probably a servant or a kinsman. And if they weren't that, they were probably an awakened human with the powers of vanquishing these creatures of evil.

We eventually theorized there is only one person left who is so stunningly normal and boring that he has no idea that the supernatural world exists and probably even disables it temporarily by being in the vicinity… Which kindof made him supernatural anyway.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
“Dammit!” the Critic shouted. “How many times have I said not to fucking do that? What is the fucking point of making work that kills anyone who looks at it? The whole damn point of art is to send a message! How the hell can your audience get anything from a piece when it rips their heads off and shoves it in their asses or some shit? That’s not art, it’s fucking bullshit!”

After a few moments, the artist quavered, “s-so… I should make it so the button gets rid of people whose art killed people?”

This is where I upvoted. though the whole thing is brilliant and hillarious.

item.title: Authorialistical Commenterationings
item.content:encoded: So, I was reading 048-J, and I saw that the number of onsite personnel killed in the first log must have been at least one billion people, which meant that at least a seventh of the world's population worked for the Foundation. Then I remembered a certain user who always said that they disliked the GOI's because it made the world so crowded with anomalies that it would've been impossible to keep it all a secret. Two hours later I had this.
